description: Intersect keeps the steps of an explanation whose node another explanation also selects, in the first explanation's order
code:
price = 10
quantity = 3
rate = 0.2
subtotal = price * quantity
tax = subtotal * rate
shipping = quantity * 2 + price
(why tax |> intersect(why shipping)).map(step -> step.node)

description: Except keeps what one explanation rests on and another does not
code:
fan = 2
load = 40
current = load * 2
heat = current + fan
noise = fan * 10
(why heat |> except(why noise)).map(step -> step.node)

description: Intersecting two impact selections gives what both inputs move
code:
price = 10
rate = 0.2
subtotal = price * 3
tax = subtotal * rate
total = subtotal + tax
fee = rate * 5
(affects price |> intersect(affects rate)).map(step -> step.node)

description: A state filter keeps the same steps before or after intersect
code:
a = 1
b = 2
c = a + b
d = c * 2
e = b + 5
[(why d |> stated |> intersect(why e)).map(step -> step.node), (why d |> intersect(why e) |> stated).map(step -> step.node)]

description: A depth stage keeps the same steps before or after intersect, because intersect keeps each step's distance
code:
x = 1
y = x + 1
z = y * 2
w = z + x
[(why w |> depth(1) |> intersect(why z)).map(step -> step.node), (why w |> intersect(why z) |> depth(1)).map(step -> step.node)]

description: A walk after intersect starts from the steps the intersection kept
code:
price = 10
quantity = 3
subtotal = price * quantity
shipping = quantity * 2
label = shipping + 1
(why subtotal |> intersect(why shipping) |> affects).map(step -> step.node)

description: A standing intersection follows a rule rewired on the other side
code:
a = 1
b = 2
left = a + 1
right = b + 1
common = why left |> intersect(why right)
right = a + b
common.map(step -> step.node)

description: Except with a reference drops only that node, and intersect with model keeps every step
code:
price = 10
quantity = 3
tax = price * quantity
[(why tax |> except(tax)).map(step -> step.node), (why tax |> intersect(model)).length]

description: A name that holds a selection is a reasoning observer, so it selects nothing as the other selection; the pipeline is written in place
code:
price = 10
tax = price * 2
shipping = price + 1
causes = why shipping
[(why tax |> intersect(causes)).length, (why tax |> intersect(why shipping)).length]

description: A class-level rule gives every instance its own intersection
code:
class Item(price, qty, fee):
    this.price = price
    this.qty = qty
    this.fee = fee
$Item.total = $Item.price * $Item.qty
$Item.cost = $Item.qty + $Item.fee
$Item.shared = why $Item.total |> intersect(why $Item.cost)
pen = Item(2, 5, 1)
cup = Item(3, 1, 4)
[pen.shared.map(step -> step.node), cup.shared.map(step -> step.node)]
